entities.summary:
Baron Nikola Jurišić was a Croatian nobleman, soldier, and diplomat who commanded a force with fewer than 50 soldiers and only 700 villagers during the Siege of Kőszeg against a much larger Ottoman army of 120,000–140,000, stopping its advance.

Born in 1490 in Senj, Croatia, Jurišić rose to prominence as a military leader and politician in the 16th-century Balkans.

Despite being vastly outnumbered, Jurišić's strategic thinking and bravery allowed him to hold off the Ottoman forces, earning him recognition as a hero in Croatia.

His legacy extends beyond the Siege of Kőszeg, as it marked a significant turning point in the region's history, highlighting the resilience of local populations against overwhelming odds.

The Siege of Kőszeg also underscores the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers and the Ottoman Empire during this period.

Jurišić's actions during the siege have been praised by historians as a testament to the ingenuity and determination of Croatian resistance against the Ottoman Empire's expansion into Eastern Europe.

As a symbol of Croatian patriotism and a champion of local self-defense, Baron Nikola Jurišić remains an important figure in Croatian history and a reminder of the importance of preserving national identity and cultural heritage.

This remarkable story serves as a powerful example of how individual courage and strategic thinking can shape the course of history, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
